mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in a month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days after qualifying employment growth, or the effect is present only in contractionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,200 in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating stronger consumer demand momentum.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day forward return when HOUST crosses above 1200, or the effect is absent in post-crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% coincides with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in a month
failure_condition: INDPRO declines but SPX 20-day returns are positive, or the effect is not robust across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS < 2% (below historical averages) create an interaction effect with GDPC1 (GDP demand), producing a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return via lower discounting and stronger demand.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for two consecutive months AND GDPC1 rising
failure_condition: No significant positive 5-day forward return when both conditions hold, or interaction coefficient <0.05 in OLS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment) below 4.5% triggers a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to market anticipation of tighter labor conditions and possible rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite UNRATE decline, or effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in tightening phases.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales of autos) falls by more than 10% in a month, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative due to weak auto demand and broader sector weakness.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: Auto sales decline but SPX 20-day return is positive, or effect is not robust across multiple recessions.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 3%, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative as markets anticipate rate hikes and discount future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive despite high inflation, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in high-inflation episodes.
